title: Show HN: I put employees inside S&P 500 market-cap bubbles
content:
I was playing around with visualising the S&P 500 by market cap and decided to add employees to each company's bubble.
What surprised me was how empty some of the biggest companies looked.
Nvidia is worth $5.2 trillion but employs only 42,000 people. That's around $124 million in market cap per employee. Meanwhile, Accenture employs 814,000 people and is worth $146 billion.
Each stick figure represents 10,000 employees. You can zoom in and explore individual companies.
I wrote a bit more about what I found here: https://bigwhalehunting.com/blog/workforce/ 
Would be interested to hear what you think.

title: Show HN: Freehire, open-source search 3M+ tech jobs from company career boards
content:
freehire is a filterable, job board aggregator, job tracker, and AI-assisted resume tailoring tool. Saving your skills and preferences changes which jobs appear and how your resume gets tailored. title: Referat: Private Meeting Notes
content:
Record meetings, get the minutes: speakers, summary, action items. On-device.

Referat records your meetings and writes the minutes. Tap record, and Referat writes down who said what, gives every speaker a name and makes a short summary with the decisions and action items. Audio never leaves your iPhone.
 How it works
 Tap record. Recording keeps going with the screen locked, and you can mark a moment to come back to.
 Read the transcript with speaker names, or the summary with decisions and who does what.
 Copy the summary into an email, or export it as text, PDF or subtitles.
 What's inside
 A transcript with a name for every speaker; the text follows along as you listen
 A short summary, the decisions and action items you can tick off
 Search across every meeting you've recorded
 Import audio files and voice memos
 Transcribes English, Danish, German, French, Spanish, Japanese and Korean
 No minute limits
 Private by design
 Transcription and speaker labels run on the iPhone (Whisper and pyannote models), and summaries use Apple's on-device model (iOS 26 with Apple Intelligence). Audio is never uploaded. No account, no ads, no tracking.
 Free
 Every feature is free. If you like it, an optional Supporter purchase adds a few extra app icons. Nothing is ever locked.

title: CrowdGPT - A collaboratively trained LLM.
content:
Hello, I'm developing CrowdGPT , a project aiming to create an LLM without datacenters and without the usual millions of dollars spent by AI companies.
 The project aims to train a 1 billion parameter model collaboratively and openly, with a protocol where everyone gets a say in the direction the project takes. Anyone can use their PC to train the AI independently, then add their contributions to the global model.
 Unlike most American and Chinese AI companies, the project is not only open-source, but also makes 100% of its training data public (along with the weights). Anyone can submit their own clean data to train the model, and even help steer the project in new directions. This creates the paradigm of an AI we all have a stake in.
 The project is open to as many people as possible, which is why I'd like to ask: what's stopping you from contributing to the project? I want to hear your answers so I can improve it. Are people simply willing to dedicate some of their GPU time to training a cool new open-source model? Or do they want something in return (like free inference credits on the crowdgpt model for example)?
 Although the current model is somewhat small (1 billion parameters), I plan to make it bigger / better in the future, and its current size is only meant as a proof of concept.
 Any advice / feedback on the project is welcome.
 Here's the project website: https://www.crowdgpt.net/ 
 Or the GitHub if anyone wants to check out the code 😂 https://github.com/Vxtzq/CrowdGPT 
 Thanks in advance.
 PS: I hope this post follows the subreddit's rules! My main goal is to gather criticism and understand how to make the project more accessible, not to advertise it 😅

title: Badgey
content: Your iPhone becomes a name badge that faces the room · Badgey turns your iPhone into a name badge. On a lanyard, it turns to face the people you meet and swings as you move. In a chest pocket, it shrinks so your name shows above the edge. Several badges, a QR code for your link, five designs.

top_comments.author: [REDACTED]
top_comments.text:
Hi everyone, I'm Marco. I make small iPhone apps on my own.

Badgey turns your iPhone into a name badge. Clip the phone to a lanyard and turn it upside down: the badge turns round to face the people in front of you and swings a little as you walk. Slide it top first into a chest pocket and it shrinks to a strip, so your name shows above the edge.

The pocket check uses the front camera for a few seconds while the phone is upside down. A small model on the phone decides, and the frames are never stored.

You can keep several badges (work, a conference, a meetup), add a link that turns into a QR code on the back, and choose a design: Classic, Office, Event, Minimal or Live, which moves. It's free with one badge; Pro is a one-time purchase.

I'd love to hear where you'd wear it, and what's missing.

title: git-flow-next
content: Your favorite Git workflow. Reimagined. · A flexible, modern approach to the popular git-flow branching model. Download the CLI tool to get started with a better Git workflow: brew install git-flow-next

Thanks so much for hunting us, @fmerian! 🙌

Hey Product Hunt 👋 I'm Bruno from the Tower team, and we also work on git-flow-next.

git-flow-next is the successor to the original git-flow, the branching model that has organized feature, release and hotfix branches for countless teams since 2010. We rebuilt it from scratch in Go, and it's fully compatible with your existing git-flow setups. It's free and open source, and it's endorsed by Vincent Driessen, the creator of git-flow, which means a lot to us.
